functions.sqlite3_memory_alarm: `sqlite3_memory_alarm` is a stub here: it accepts a callback, arg, and memory threshold, but ignores them all and always returns `SQLITE_OK`. It has no effect and should not be relied on for alarms in this build.
functions.sqlite3_str_finish: `sqlite3_str_finish()` ends a `sqlite3_str` builder, frees the object, and returns the built string buffer. Use the result with `sqlite3_free()`. It returns `NULL` if `p` is NULL/OOM sentinel, on construction errors, or if the string is empty.
functions.sqlite3_busy_timeout: Sets the connection’s busy handler to wait/retry on locks for up to `ms` ms, then make `sqlite3_step()` return `SQLITE_BUSY`. `ms<=0` disables busy handling. It replaces any prior busy handler; one per connection.
functions.sqlite3_close_v2: `sqlite3_close_v2()` closes a database handle, but unlike `sqlite3_close()` it can be called even if prepared statements/blobs are still open. The handle is closed immediately if possible; otherwise it becomes invalid and is finalized when the remaining objects are closed.
functions.sqlite3_file_control: `sqlite3_file_control()` is a low-level hook to issue file-control ops on a specific DB file. Use `main`/`temp`/ATTACH name (or NULL for main). Some opcodes are handled by SQLite and return pointers/data; unknown DB name gives `SQLITE_ERROR`, and xFileControl’s return is passed through.
functions.sqlite3_result_value: `sqlite3_result_value()` sets a SQL function’s result to the exact value in `sqlite3_value*`. Use it in a user-defined function with a valid `sqlite3_context`. It copies the value into the result; no conversion or special-case logic is shown here.
functions.sqlite3_unlock_notify: `sqlite3_unlock_notify()` registers a callback for a blocked connection after `SQLITE_LOCKED` in shared-cache mode. Use it to be notified when the blocking transaction ends. If no blocker exists, callback fires immediately; NULL cancels; deadlocks return `SQLITE_LOCKED`.
functions.sqlite3_mutex_notheld: `sqlite3_mutex_notheld()` is a mutex debug/check helper. It tests whether `p` is **not** held by the current thread. Use it only for assertions or diagnostics. It returns true if `p==0` or if the mutex subsystem reports it is not held; otherwise false.
functions.sqlite3_db_mutex:
`sqlite3_db_mutex()` returns the mutex protecting a `sqlite3*` connection in Serialized mode. Use it only to access/check the connection’s mutex; in Single-thread or Multi-thread mode it returns `NULL`. With API armor, an invalid `db` returns `NULL` (misuse).
Use sqlite3_db_mutex() only as an observation/synchronization aid around a valid open sqlite3* handle, and only in accordance with SQLite's threading mode. Do not blindly call sqlite3_mutex_try() on the returned mutex after operations that may already hold it internally. If used, check that the database connection was opened successfully and avoid re-entrant locking patterns on non-recursive database mutexes.
functions.sqlite3_bind_int64: Binds a 64-bit signed integer to parameter `i` of prepared stmt `pStmt`. Call with a valid bind index (1-based). It first unbinds any prior value; on `SQLITE_OK` it stores `iValue` and releases the DB mutex. Returns the unbind result.
functions.sqlite3_shutdown: `sqlite3_shutdown()` cleanly deinitializes SQLite’s global subsystems. Call it after all DB connections are closed, before process exit or before reinitializing SQLite. It shuts down OS, pcache, malloc, and extensions if initialized; repeated calls are safe/no-op when already off.
functions.sqlite3_value_text: `sqlite3_value_text()` returns the UTF-8 text representation of a `sqlite3_value*`. Use it to read a value as text in user-defined functions/collations. It may convert from other types; if conversion fails, it returns `NULL`.
functions.sqlite3_vtab_config: `sqlite3_vtab_config()` lets a virtual table’s `xConnect`/`xCreate` set per-module flags on the current DB connection. Use only there; outside that context it returns `SQLITE_MISUSE`. `CONSTRAINT_SUPPORT` sets `bConstraint`, `INNOCUOUS`/`DIRECTONLY` set risk flags.
functions.sqlite3_wal_hook: Registers a per-connection WAL commit hook. It replaces any prior hook and returns the old `pArg`. The callback runs after each WAL commit, after the write-lock is released, gets `(pArg, db, dbname, nPages)`, and should usually return `SQLITE_OK`.
functions.sqlite3_column_database_name: Returns the source database name for result column N of a prepared SELECT. Use on a prepared stmt, 0-based column index. Returns original unaliased db name, or NULL for expressions/subqueries, no metadata build, or on error. Valid until finalize/reprepare.
functions.sqlite3_stmt_readonly: Returns whether a prepared stmt makes any direct DB-file changes. Use it to detect read-only vs potentially writing SQL. It may still return true for side-effect writes via functions/virtual tables, and false for statements that might write even if they end up no-op.
functions.sqlite3_result_error_nomem: `sqlite3_result_error_nomem()` reports an out-of-memory failure from a user-defined SQL function. Call it with the current `sqlite3_context*`. It sets the result to NULL, marks the context as `SQLITE_NOMEM_BKPT`, and flags the DB OOM fault.
functions.sqlite3_transfer_bindings: Transfers bound parameter values from `pFromStmt` to `pToStmt`. Use it when both prepared statements have the same number of parameters; otherwise it returns `SQLITE_ERROR`. If either stmt is expired, it marks it expired before copying bindings.
functions.sqlite3_stmt_status: Returns a prepared statement’s selected status counter, optionally resetting it. Use it to inspect performance/behavior (eg scans, steps). `SQLITE_STMTSTATUS_MEMUSED` is special: it reports memory used and frees the statement object.
functions.sqlite3_prepare16_v3: `sqlite3_prepare16_v3` prepares a UTF-16 SQL string into a compiled `sqlite3_stmt*`. It always adds `SQLITE_PREPARE_SAVESQL`, passes through only valid `prepFlags`, and returns a status code. On success `*ppStmt` is set; `pzTail` points to unparsed SQL.
